inputs.source: Customer support ticket / inbound email body

instructions.note: The agent may look up any customer by email or account id, with no check that the id belongs to the person emailing.
Direct, unattended sending of a 'routine' reply can conflict with the line 14 restriction if a request that discloses another customer's data is misclassified as routine.
The sole protection against cross-customer disclosure is a prompt instruction; no structural control (credential scoping, recipient binding, approval gate) enforces it.
The agent acts without human review for any ticket it judges 'routine,' and escalates only on its own sentiment judgment of 'angry,' which is not a structural gate.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Enforcement depends entirely on the model choosing to follow the instruction. A more capable or manipulated model can rationalize an exception, or be talked into one by text in the inbound email.

controls.name: Escalate to a human only when the customer appears angry
controls.decay_rationale: The escalation trigger is itself a model judgment of sentiment, not a structural gate. An attacker can keep tone neutral while requesting cross-customer data, and a more capable model is not thereby more likely to escalate.

controls.name: Outbound email logged to SIEM
controls.decay_rationale: Logging is enforced outside the model and does not decay with capability, but it is detective only: it does not prevent disclosure, it records it after the email has already left the boundary.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to the ticket's system-of-record requester
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Deriving the send destination from the ticket record rather than from model-chosen input would sever the path to arbitrary recipients.

controls.name: Per-ticket CRM credential scoped to the requesting customer's own record
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record today; scoping it to the ticket's own customer would make cross-customer reads structurally impossible.

controls.name: Human approval gate before sends disclosing CRM data to a non-verified recipient
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. The agent sends routine replies with no human in the loop.

controls.name: MCP tool definition pinning/hashing for crm_mcp and mail_mcp
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. mcp.json shows no hash or version pin for either server's tool definitions, so descriptions or schemas could change after review.

controls.name: Mutual TLS or signed identity for MCP server authentication
controls.decay_rationale: Only static bearer tokens are configured; a leaked token is indistinguishable from a legitimate call, and this weakens further as more servers and tools are added.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1) via over-broad CRM credential (TC4): untrusted email drives arbitrary customer lookup and unattended send

attack_path.note: Untrusted customer email can specify any account id/email and an implicit return address for the agent's reply.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record; prompt.md:3 permits lookup by any email or account id with no binding to the sender's own identity.
MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address; prompt.md:5-6 sends routine replies directly with no human review.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model or platform version string changes without a separate review (subject.model.swappable is true), or prompt.md line 14 / the anger-escalation clause is edited, weakened, or removed.

evidence.observation: Agent looks up the customer with get_customer and 'may look up any customer by email or account id,' with no check that the id belongs to the sender.
'If the answer is routine, send it directly with send. Do not wait for a human unless the customer is angry' — unattended send with no approval gate.
'Never share another customer's information with the person emailing you' is the only stated control against cross-customer disclosure, and it is behavioral only.
crm_mcp and mail_mcp both authenticate with static bearer tokens; no credential scoping is shown in the connection config.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record. MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address.

recommendations.action: Scope the CRM credential per ticket to the requesting customer's own record, derived from the authenticated ticket rather than from agent-chosen input.
Bind the send recipient to the ticket's system-of-record requester address; disallow agent-chosen recipients.
Add a raw-action human approval gate before any send that would disclose CRM data to a recipient other than the ticket's verified requester.

findings.title: Unpinned, statically authenticated MCP servers enable tool definition tampering (ASI04)

attack_path.note: Static bearer token auth (CRM_SVC_TOKEN), no peer identity verification or definition pinning is stated.
Static bearer token auth (MAIL_SVC_TOKEN), no peer identity verification or definition pinning is stated.

forecast.watch_signal: Addition of further MCP servers without pinning or mutual TLS, or any further loosening of token handling for crm_mcp / mail_mcp.

evidence.observation: Both MCP servers are configured with only a static Authorization bearer header; no mutual TLS, signed identity, or definition hash/pin is specified.
No mention of tool definition pinning or peer identity verification for either crm_mcp or mail_mcp.

Tier assigned by judgment as a supply-chain/infrastructure-trust finding rather than a formal input-to-capability path: treated analogously to an internal-trust source reaching an irreversible-egress sink. The autonomy modifier was not applied because this path does not depend on the agent's unattended step or runtime behavior.

recommendations.action: Pin or hash crm_mcp and mail_mcp tool definitions and alert on drift.
Replace static bearer tokens with mutual TLS or signed server identity for both MCP connections.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical because an untrusted inbound email can drive an unscoped CRM read (broad credential, any account id) into an unattended, irreversible send through a shared mail service account that can reach any address (f1), and separately because both MCP servers rely on static tokens with no definition pinning (f2). The only controls in place today are a prompt instruction and a sentiment-based escalation heuristic, both behavioral and dependent on the model, which bring residual to high rather than lower; no structural control severs the path, so the floor stops at high per the rubric's credit caps. The forecast returns to critical because the model is explicitly upgraded with the platform with no separate review (subject.model.swappable = true), and model_upgrade or simple control_removal (editing the prompt) defeats both credited controls, fully reopening the inherent path.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.
No tool manifest or MCP server-side schema beyond the connection config was provided; the exact parameters and bounds of get_customer and send are inferred from the system prompt and runtime notes.
No agent card, approval-workflow configuration, or infrastructure-as-code was provided; autonomy level and the absence of approval gates are inferred from the system prompt alone.
